s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with chest pain and ECG changes
salient_findings: Dull chest pain of 2 hours' duration
ST segment depression >1mm in V2 and V3
New discordant ST elevation of 1mm in leads II, III, and aVF
key_facts: Male patient in his 70s
History of coronary artery bypass surgery
Ejection fraction of 25%
Biventricular pacemaker placement
ECG shows sinus activity at 72 beats/min
QRS duration of 160 milliseconds
Ventricular depolarization preceded by 2 pacing stimuli
Initial troponin negative 2 hours after symptom onset
Cardiac catheterization revealed thrombotic occlusion of saphenous vein graft
Occlusive lesions in proximal obtuse marginal artery

raw.champion: Acute coronary syndrome with graft involvement
raw.rationale: The patient's history of coronary artery bypass surgery, ECG findings of ST segment depression and new discordant ST elevation, and cardiac catheterization revealing thrombotic occlusion of saphenous vein graft and occlusive lesions in native coronary arteries support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Initial troponin was negative 2 hours after symptom onset, which does not strongly support acute myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: Unstable angina
rejected.why: The presence of ST elevation and thrombotic occlusion of saphenous vein graft suggests a more severe condition than unstable angina.

rejected.label: Saphenous vein graft disease
rejected.why: While the patient has saphenous vein graft disease, this diagnosis alone does not fully explain the acute presentation and ECG findings.

rejected.label: Native coronary artery disease
rejected.why: The patient's native coronary artery disease is likely a contributing factor, but the acute presentation is more directly related to the graft involvement.
